Russia Says It Will Open Humanitarian Corridor to Trapped Ukrainian Town of Oleshky

29 Oct 2026, 08:21 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.npr.org

Image: www.npr.org — Creative Commons

Key takeawaysRussia and Ukraine have agreed to a very limited ceasefire to establish a humanitarian corridor for the occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, where roughly 2,000 remaining residents have faced extreme deprivation and isolation for nearly five years. Located on the Dnipro

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a very limited ceasefire to establish a humanitarian corridor for the occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, where roughly 2,000 remaining residents have faced extreme deprivation and isolation for nearly five years.

Located on the Dnipro River in southern Ukraine, Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022. Russian forces heavily mined the surrounding land, cutting off regular supplies of food and medicine and trapping the local population.

Dire Conditions Inside Oleshky

Family members and exiled officials report severe humanitarian conditions inside the town. Residents have subsisted on homemade vegetable pickles and soups made from grass and weeds. The town suffers from a lack of electricity, running water, and basic medical supplies.

Civilians also face severe dangers from land mines and active drones. According to accounts relayed by family members outside the area, movement is strictly limited, and retrieving the bodies of deceased neighbors has been rendered exceptionally dangerous.

International Appeals and Ceasefire Agreement

Public awareness campaigns and protests have taken place in Ukraine, including demonstrations outside the Vatican's embassy in Kyiv. International figures, including Pope Leo and First Lady Melania Trump, previously urged action to establish corridors for food, medicine, and evacuations.

Following these appeals, both Ukraine and Russia announced an agreement on a ceasefire for Oleshky. Residents have been informed that evacuation efforts are slated to begin with buses transporting individuals to a shut-down children's camp, though long-term plans remain unclear.

Practical Implications and Verification

  • Confirmed Facts: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a limited ceasefire for Oleshky. Approximately 2,000 residents remain trapped due to surrounding minefields and military occupation since 2022.
  • What Remains Unknown: The long-term destination and safety provisions for evacuees beyond the initial transfer to a closed children's camp are currently unspecified.
  • User Impact: Families with relatives inside the occupied town face ongoing uncertainty as evacuation procedures begin.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review the original reporting and updates through the official [NPR Source Report](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/26/nx-s1-6014540/russia-says-it-will-open-humanitarian-corridor-to-ukrainian-town).
